title: Per-route adaptive thresholds and guarded apply for per-customer batching/caching recommendations
creator: Anika Bose
description: Deliver a safe control-plane flow that converts telemetry-driven batching and KV-caching recommendations into per-customer and per-route configuration changes. The flow must score candidates (cost benefit, latency risk, quality risk), group customers into adaptive segments, expose allowlist/denylist overrides, and apply changes behind guarded policies that support dry-run, canary, and automated rollback based on SLOs and quality regressions. Focus is on minimizing unit cost without violating latency and correctness constraints.
acceptance_criteria: Automated recommendation engine produces per-route candidate changes with metadata: expected cost delta, expected latency delta, confidence score, synthetic QA delta estimate
Segmentation engine assigns customers to dynamic tiers (e.g., safe, conservative, experimental) with stable rules and manual overrides
Allowlist/denylist UI-backed API exists to pin customers or routes to specific policy buckets
Guarded apply supports: dry-run (shadow traffic), canary (1-5% traffic), ramp with metric gating, automated rollback when thresholds exceeded
Rollout and rollback events are emitted to the Console and appear in the runtime cost/latency dashboards
End-to-end test harness validates that canary rollback happens when 95th latency increases > 20ms or QA regression > 0.5% absolute on synthetic prompt set
implementation_notes: Recommendation scorer: weighted score = alpha*cost_saving - beta*latency_risk - gamma*qa_risk; alpha/beta/gamma are runtime-configurable
Segmentation: deterministic hashing of customer_id + route to assign stable buckets; support rule overrides (tags: enterprise, beta-customer, privacy-sensitive)
Policy engine: evaluate allowlist/denylist prior to automated apply; denylist prevents any automation; allowlist promotes to aggressive bucket
Safe apply controller: three-phase apply (shadow -> canary -> ramp) with metric probes at each phase; metrics pulled from Console telemetry endpoints
Rollback controller: two modes: immediate (hard threshold breach) and adaptive (trend-based rollback if 3 consecutive evaluation windows show degradation)
State persistence: store candidate proposals and rollout history in policy-store (immutable records) for audit and for Console timelines
testing_plan: Unit tests for scorer math and tie-breaking behavior
Integration tests: simulate mixed customer traffic to exercise segmentation and allowlist logic
Chaos test: inject GPU contention to ensure guarded apply detects latency increases and triggers rollback
Regression QA: run synthetic prompt set against baseline and candidate models/configs to compute quality delta; gating thresholds enforced in CI
E2E canary test in staging: shadow traffic for 24h, then 2% canary for 6h with automated checks
rollout_strategy: Phase 0 - Dry run: all proposals executed in shadow mode for 48h; collect cost/latency/QA telemetry
Phase 1 - Canary: pick subset of safe-tier customers (1-2% traffic) for 6h windows; if metrics within thresholds, continue
Phase 2 - Incremental ramp: 2x traffic every 12h until target percentage reached; metric checks before each increment
Fallback: if metric gates fail, immediate rollback to previous config for the affected customers/routes and notify on-call
Manual override: Console UI button to abort or accelerate rollout for enterprise customers
rollback_plan: Immediate rollback when: 95th latency increases by >20ms OR error rate increases by >0.2% absolute OR QA regression >0.5% absolute
Adaptive rollback: if trending degradation over 3 windows (each window = 1h) with statistical significance p<0.05
Rollback steps: mark candidate as failed, revert policy-store entry, issue remediation PR to infra if hotfix required, notify stakeholders via Slack/Email
Postmortem: auto-open incident ticket with attached telemetry snapshots from before/after the apply
